title: Acute abdominal pain: aorta, gallbladder, kidneys and bowel
summary: Six focused scans for the patient with abdominal pain: the aorta, the gallbladder, the kidneys and ureteric jets, small bowel obstruction, the appendix and, in children, intussusception. Learn what each scan rules in, what it cannot rule out, and when to escalate.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency, acute and urgent care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners and physician associates who assess adults and children with abdominal pain.
outcomes: Scan the whole abdominal aorta and recognise an aneurysm of 3 cm or more
Find the gallbladder using the main lobar fissure and recognise the signs of cholecystitis
Grade hydronephrosis, separate it from its mimics, and use ureteric jets in suspected renal colic
Recognise small bowel obstruction and the features of complications
Recognise appendicitis and intussusception, and act safely on a non-diagnostic scan
